'''Leona Ann Harris''' is an American mathematician who is the Director of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) at the [[American Mathematical Society|American Mathematical Society (AMS)]]. She was the executive director of the [[National Association of Mathematicians|National Association of Mathematicians (NAM)]] from 2019 to 2022.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=News from the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6918 |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Harris earned a [[Bachelor of Science|bachelor of science]] degree in mathematics from [[Spelman College]] in 1995, graduating [[magna cum laude]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Etta Z. Falconer Lecture Series {{!}} Spelman College |url=https://www.spelman.edu/academics/majors-and-programs/mathematics/falconer-lecture-series |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=www.spelman.edu}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/leona-harris/|title=Black History Month 2019 Honoree:Leona Harris|website=Mathematically Gifted and Black|access-date=January 5, 2023}}</ref> In 2001, she earned her doctorate in applied mathematics from the [[North Carolina State University]] with the dissertation ''Differential Equation Models for the Hormonal Regulation of the Menstrual Cycle'' under the advisement of James Francis Selgrade.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leona Harris - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=67240 |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> Harris has been on the faculty at [[Bennett College]], [[The College of New Jersey]], [[Georgetown University]], [[Marymount University]], and the [[University of the District of Columbia]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2022 |title=People News for March 2022 {{!}} Amstat News |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/03/01/people-news-for-march-2022/ |access-date=June 24, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> Harris had the rank of associate professor at The College of New Jersey and at the University of the District of Columbia where she also served as chair of the Division of Sciences and Mathematics.<ref name=":0" /> Prior to her current role at the AMS, she worked as a program analyst in the Office of Science at the [[Center for Tobacco Products]] of the [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]]. She served as the executive director of the [[National Association of Mathematicians|National Association of Mathematicians (NAM)]] from 2019 to 2022, and was the organization's interim president from June 2020 to January 2021.<ref name=":2" />

Harris, along with [[Tanya Moore (activist)|Tanya Moore]] and [[Nagambal Shah]], started the Infinite Possibilities Conferences which was "created to educate, empower and create new frontiers by building on the undaunted spirit of women in the mathematical sciences."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Infinite Possibilities Conference - Building Diversity in Science |url=https://www.diversityinscience.org/infinite-possibilities-conference/ |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=www.diversityinscience.org}}</ref> She was an instructor for the [[EDGE Foundation|EDGE]] program in 2008<ref>{{Cite web |title=EDGE for women 2008 people |url=https://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-2008/ |access-date=June 24, 2022}}</ref> and 2018<ref>{{Cite web |title=EDGE for Women 2018 participants |url=https://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-2018-participants/ |access-date=June 24, 2022}}</ref> which helps women get advanced degrees in mathematics and was co-editor of the book ''A Celebration of the EDGE Program’s Impact on the Mathematics Community and Beyond'' published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-19486-4 |title=A Celebration of the EDGE Program's Impact on the Mathematics Community and Beyond |series=Association for Women in Mathematics Series |year=2019 |volume=18 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-19486-4|isbn=978-3-030-19485-7 |s2cid=235943340 }}</ref> In 2022, Harris was chosen to give the [[Etta Zuber Falconer|Etta Z. Falconer]] Lecture at Spelman College; the title of her lecture was ''The Making of a Mathematician Through Inspiration, Empowerment, and Mentorship: Reflections on My Mathematical Journey''.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Harris's mother, Teresa Dawn Edwards, also graduated from [[Spelman College]] with a degree in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of the African Diaspora Harris profile |url=https://www.mathad.com/profile?bfjg2518292543703786659hdcg }}</ref>  Edwards has a PhD in [[Industrial and Systems Engineering|Industrial & Systems Engineering]] from the [[Georgia Tech|Georgia Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of African Diaspora Edwards Profile |url=https://www.mathad.com/profile?ifbd2518292545117251218jbaf |access-date=June 24, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Teresa Edwards - Mathematician of the African Diaspora |url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/edwards_teresa.html |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref>
